ideas.name: UmbraPath
ideas.problem: Standard GPS algorithms optimize for speed and distance, ignoring the 'thermal cost' of walking through unshaded, high-heat urban corridors, which can lead to heat exhaustion and discomfort during heatwaves.
ideas.targetUser: Urban commuters, elderly pedestrians, and parents with strollers in dense, high-heat metropolitan areas.
coreFeatures: Shade-First Routing: A navigation engine that prioritizes paths with maximum tree canopy and building shadow coverage over the shortest distance.
Dynamic Shadow Forecasting: Predictive modeling that adjusts suggested routes based on the sun's angle at the user's specific departure time.
Live Thermal Heatmap: A real-time visual overlay showing street-level temperature variances and 'heat island' hotspots.
Cool-Spot Reporting: A community-driven feature allowing users to pin active misting stations, public fountains, or extra-dense canopy zones.
realDependencies: Google Maps Directions API
OpenWeatherMap API
City-provided GIS/LiDAR data (for building height and tree canopy mapping)
SunCalc library for solar position modeling
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'Mock-City.json' file containing a set of predefined waypoints, each with hardcoded 'shade_index' (0.0-1.0) and 'ambient_temp' values. To simulate real-time sun movement, a 'Time Slider' will be implemented; as the user moves the slider, a mathematical function will adjust the 'shade_index' of waypoints using a sine wave to mimic the sun's arc across the sky. All 'API requests' will be wrapped in a wrapper function that returns these local JSON objects after a randomized delay of 800ms to 2000ms to simulate network latency and loading states.

ideas.name: PagePeek
ideas.niche: Hyper-local book exchange inventory and maintenance tracking
ideas.problem: The frustration of traveling to a Little Free Library only to find it empty, poorly curated, or physically damaged/weather-beaten.
ideas.targetUser: Avid readers, local community organizers, and parents looking for specific children's genres who reside in walkable or bikeable neighborhoods.
coreFeatures: Live Genre Tally: Users tap quick-count buttons (e.g., +1 Sci-Fi, +1 Mystery) to update stock levels instantly.
Condition Health Meter: A community-driven status indicator (Excellent, Dusty, Wet/Damaged, or Empty).
Genre-Filtered Discovery Map: An interactive map allowing users to filter nearby boxes by specific genres like 'YA', 'Non-Fiction', or 'Children's'.
Stock Alerts: Push notifications when a user's 'Wishlist Genre' is spotted in a box within a 2-mile radius.
Stewardship Mode: A dedicated interface for box owners to mark their library as 'Recently Restocked' or 'Needs Maintenance'.
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Maps SDK & Places API)
Firebase Firestore (Real-time NoSQL database)
Cloudinary API (Image hosting for box condition photos)
Firebase Cloud Messaging (Push notifications)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local `mockDatabase.json` containing 30 pre-defined library objects with realistic coordinates, timestamps, and genre arrays. To simulate real-time connectivity, all data fetching will be wrapped in a custom `useMockFetch` hook that injects a randomized delay (500ms to 1800ms) and a 'Loading...' state. To emulate 'live' community activity, a `setInterval` function will trigger every 30 seconds to randomly update the 'stockCount' or 'condition' of one library in the mock array, causing the UI to re-render as if a real user had just submitted an update. Photo uploads will be simulated by displaying a progress bar that transitions from 0% to 100% before swapping a placeholder icon with a static local image URL.

ideas.name: StashScout
ideas.niche: Hyperlocal micro-retail 'New Arrival' discovery for niche enthusiasts.
ideas.problem: Niche hobbyists miss rare, hard-to-find items because they rely on fragmented social media stories from small boutiques, which are easily missed and lack searchable, item-specific notification capabilities.
ideas.targetUser: Dedicated collectors and hobbyists (ages 25–55) with high discretionary income, such as indie book collectors, specialty yarn enthusiasts, or vinyl aficionados, who live in urban/suburban areas and prioritize small businesses over Amazon.
coreFeatures: Niche Watchlists: Users follow specific item tags (e.g., 'hand-dyed merino' or 'signed first editions') rather than just stores.
Merchant 'Snap-to-Post': A streamlined mobile interface for owners to take a photo and tag an item for instant broadcast.
Geo-Fenced Proximity Alerts: Real-time push notifications triggered when a watched item arrives within a user-defined radius.
Instant Hold: A one-tap 'Reserve for 24h' button that sends a priority request to the boutique.
realDependencies: Google Maps Places API (for store location and geofencing)
Firebase Cloud Messaging (for real-time push notifications)
Cloudinary API (for optimized merchant image hosting)
Twilio API (for SMS fallback notifications)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'Simulation Engine' class that periodically injects randomized 'New Arrival' events into the application state to mimic real-world merchant activity. To fake the Merchant Upload, the UI will show a progress bar with a 3-second `setTimeout` before transitioning to a 'Success' state. Geolocation will be emulated by a local utility that calculates distances between the user's 'mock current location' and a hardcoded array of 'Local Boutique' coordinates. All network requests will be intercepted by a Mock Service Worker (MSW) returning pre-defined JSON payloads with simulated latency to mimic real API round-trips.

ideas.name: PurePath
ideas.niche: Community-verified real-time hygiene monitoring for municipal amenities.
ideas.problem: The unpredictable cleanliness and functional reliability of public facilities like restrooms, drinking fountains, and park benches, causing anxiety and inconvenience for sensitive demographics.
ideas.targetUser: Parents of young children, long-distance travelers, outdoor enthusiasts, and individuals with medical or hygiene-related accessibility requirements.
coreFeatures: Real-time hygiene-coded interactive map
One-tap status reporting (Clean, Dirty, Out of Order)
Advanced amenity filtering (ADA compliant, Baby Changing, Gender Neutral)
Community reputation system for verified reporters
Live 'Cleanliness Trend' alerts for specific zones
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform or Mapbox SDK
PostGIS for spatial database queries
Firebase or Supabase for real-time data synchronization
Push Notification Service (FCM/APNs)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local GeoJSON file containing 50 pre-defined urban coordinates. A 'Simulated Traffic Engine' will run a background loop that randomly updates the 'hygiene_score' and 'status' of 5-10% of these points every 20 seconds to mimic live user reports. All API calls will be wrapped in a 'Latency Proxy' that uses a randomized setTimeout (between 400ms and 1800ms) to simulate real-world network conditions. Fake push notifications will be triggered via a scheduled event queue to simulate other users reporting issues in the immediate vicinity of the demo user.

ideas.name: PopIn
ideas.problem: The high social friction and commitment required by formal social planning, which leads to urban isolation in high-density neighborhoods.
ideas.targetUser: Urban dwellers aged 22-40, specifically remote workers, new residents, and digital nomads seeking casual, low-pressure social interaction without the need for scheduling.
coreFeatures: Single-tap 'Presence Ping' with customizable expiration timers (15, 30, or 60 mins)
Micro-Activity Tags (e.g., 'Reading', 'Coffee', 'Dog walking') to signal social availability
Ephemeral Neighborhood Map showing active, time-bound presence bubbles that vanish when timers expire
Privacy-first 'Ghost Mode' that prevents permanent location tracking or long-term profile building
realDependencies: Mapbox SDK or Google Maps API for geospatial visualization
Firebase Realtime Database or Supabase for ephemeral, low-latency state synchronization
Browser/Device Geolocation API for proximity detection
Web Push API for proximity-based notifications
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local JSON manifest containing 8 'ghost' users with randomized coordinates within a tight 500-meter radius of a fixed center point. A local JavaScript interval will act as a 'mock server clock,' decrementing the 'timeRemaining' property of each ghost ping every second and removing them from the state when they hit zero. All interactions (e.g., creating a new ping) will be processed through a simulated API wrapper that utilizes 'setTimeout' to inject a randomized latency of 800ms to 1500ms, ensuring the UI displays loading states and mimics real-world network conditions.
